claude.sample_unit: patients with type 2 diabetes (11,740 NCKUH + 20,313 NTUH)

links.outcome: Calibration slopes/intercepts and GND tests before versus after local recalibration of CHIME equations
links.effect: Recalibration improved CHIME-MI slope from 0.4747 to 0.9848 (NCKUH) and 0.3774 to 1.1060 (NTUH); all recalibrated equations had GND p-values ≥ 0.05.
links.quote: All the recalibrated risk equations showed insignificant GND test results ( p -values ≥ 0.05), suggesting satisfactory calibration.

links.outcome: External validation of risk equations on local historical EHR data against outcomes with predefined acceptance criteria
links.effect: UKPDS-OM2 had unsatisfactory discrimination (AUROC 0.57-0.65); CHIME acceptable (0.71-0.79) but calibration unsatisfactory (GND p<0.001 for most), so local validation revealed the need for adaptation.
links.quote: Overall, all the CVD risk equations from UKPDS-OM2 and the stroke risk equation from RECODe demonstrated unsatisfactory discrimination (AUROC < 0.7) for Taiwanese type 2 diabetes populations, and all the CVD risk equations from the CHIME model yielded acceptable discrimination (AUROC ≥ 0.7).

links.outcome: Model performance when applied to a new population (Taiwanese T2D) beyond original development population
links.effect: Original equations were poorly calibrated in Taiwan; CHIME slopes 0.3666-0.7982 and GND p<0.001 in most cases; UKPDS-OM2 AUROC as low as 0.5726.
links.quote: Although the risk equations from the CHIME model were developed from real-world Asian type 2 diabetes populations, the calibration of these risk equations was unsatisfactory for Taiwanese type 2 diabetes populations.

unlisted_practices: Cross-institutional recalibration using common data model without pooling patient-level data

links.effect: UKPDS-OM2 AUROC 0.5726–0.6498; RECODe 0.6579–0.8084; CHIME 0.7078–0.7907; calibration remained unsatisfactory.
links.quote: The CHIME risk equations had acceptable discrimination (AUROC: 0.71-0.79) and better calibration than that for UKPDS-OM2 and RECODe, although the calibration remained unsatisfactory.

links.effect: Local validation found CHIME acceptable discrimination but unsatisfactory calibration in Taiwanese type 2 diabetes populations.
links.quote: Although the risk equations from the CHIME model were developed from real-world Asian type 2 diabetes populations, the calibration of these risk equations was unsatisfactory for Taiwanese type 2 diabetes populations.

links.effect: NTUH lacked smoking history and hemoglobin; patients were assumed non-smokers with hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL.
links.quote: Additionally, due to the lack of smoking history and hemoglobin data in the NTUH’s EHRs, the NTUH population was assumed to be non-smokers and have a hemoglobin level of 12.5 g/dL, which is aligned with the average hemoglobin level of the NCKUH population.

screen.practice: local validation and recalibration before deployment
screen.reason: The study empirically tests local recalibration of existing clinical risk prediction models (UKPDS-OM2, RECODe, CHIME) across two hospital systems using EHRs to adapt baseline hazards and improve calibration.
